title: “You Cannot Sound Like GPT”: Signs of language discrimination and resistance in computer science publishing

bias_targets.methodology: Quantitative analysis of approximately 80,000 peer reviews using RoBERTa models to classify sentence-level critiques and praises of writing clarity, regressed against the English-speaking status of the authors' affiliated institutions (using TOEFL exemption policies as a proxy), combined with qualitative semi-structured interviews of multilingual scholars.

Panel OLS regression models evaluating the association between manuscript peer review scores (including clarity evaluations) and the geographic region or country of the authors' institutions (e.g., Asia, China), examining shifts before and after the availability of ChatGPT.
